subject: Production streaming hang — request for fallback & exec visibility
message_1_body:
Hi Vanessa,

We started seeing intermittent hangs on token streaming for our production tenant around 21:50 PST. Requests are accepted but the client sees no tokens for ~10–20s, then either resumes or the socket closes with a 504. Latency and error rate spiked on our dashboards; overall throughput dropped by ~30% for 200s windows.

Attached are a sample request trace (trace-req-9f3b.json), a server log with timestamps, and a screenshot of the client showing stalled chunks. Our SRE team (cc'd) already verified network between our proxy and the client is healthy.

Important details:
- Model: redwood/gpt-2-large-fp16-v1 (hosted)
- Endpoint: /v1/streams/generate
- Request id: req-9f3b-94a2
- Typical latency before issue: 120–160ms per token; observed stalls up to 20s

Could you please triage? We need a temporary mitigation (fallback routing, disable streaming on specific routes, or recommended proxy config) and an ETA for a root-cause. This is impacting a handful of critical sessions.

Thanks,
Jamie Park
SRE, Brightline Health
message_2_subject: Re: [PROD] Streaming responses hang intermittently — urgent
message_2_body:
Thanks for the quick report and the artifacts, Jamie — I’ve looped in Rishi (runtime) and Marissa (CS lead). We’ll stand up a short war room and propose a temporary fallback while engineering investigates.

Immediate asks:
- Rishi: can you triage the req-9f3b trace and confirm whether this looks like a backend stall (kernel/blocking) vs gateway/proxy?
- Jamie: can you confirm if disabling client-side keepalive/long-poll changes behavior (we’ve seen proxies sometimes hide chunk gaps)?

I’ll share visibility to our leadership if this looks like an availability event requiring credits/exec updates. On it now.

— Vanessa
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
message_3_subject: Re: [PROD] Streaming responses hang intermittently — urgent (initial triage)
message_3_body:
Vanessa / Marissa — I dug into the trace and logs. Quick summary:

What we see:
- The request hits the frontend and we begin token generation; KV cache population looks normal for the first ~40 tokens.
- Around token ~42 the runtime shows a long GC/compaction pause (2.5–3s) followed by a series of short pauses; client sees these as stalled chunks.
- For some requests the connection recovers; for others the frontend marks the stream idle and upstream proxy (customer side) issues 504.

Probable contributing factors:
- A quantization-related memory fallback path coupled with a synchronous GC/defragment during high-concurrency windows.
- Continuous batching/backpressure: a high mix of long sessions caused KV cache thrashing on that host pool, increasing tail latencies.

Temporary mitigations I recommend immediately (can be implemented without model changes):
1) Route Brightline traffic to a lower-utilization pool with larger KV cache (we can do a routing rule for their tenant id).
2) Disable client streaming at the gateway for their problematic route — fall back to short-polling/batched responses for now. We can toggle via per-tenant flag; this reduces live-perceived interactivity but avoids stalls.
3) Apply a quick runtime tweak to push back deferred compaction (config change) — low risk for a short window.

I’ll open a dedicated incident (INC-2829) and start a controlled repro with a mirrored load. If we confirm compaction+cache eviction as root cause, we’ll schedule a micro-release with a targeted runtime guard.

Action items assigned:
- Rishi: start mirroring load and collect perf profiles (in progress).
- Vanessa: confirm if Brightline wants the temporary routing or prefers we attempt streaming with our guard (they may want to avoid UX regressions).
- Marissa: prepare comms and potential credit options if this degrades SLAs.

— Rishi
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
message_4_subject: Re: [PROD] Streaming responses hang intermittently — mitigation and exec visibility
message_4_body:
Jamie — quick update and proposed next steps. We’ve completed an initial triage. Engineering (Rishi) suspects runtime compaction + KV cache eviction under concurrent long sessions is causing tail stalls. We can do either of the two temporary mitigations this morning:

Option A (recommended): Route your tenant to a dedicated host pool with larger KV cache and enable our deferred-compaction guard. This preserves streaming and should reduce stalls; estimated time to switch: ~30–45 minutes.
Option B: Toggle streaming -> batched responses for the affected API route. This is immediate but will change UX for users (less real-time).

Please confirm which you prefer and whether you want Redwood to proceed with routing change now. We’ll open an incident page for visibility and, per standard practice, Marissa will prepare SLA remediation language if we confirm customer impact beyond our SLO.

We’ll also include an executive note summarizing impact and remediation if you’d like that routed to your leadership.

Thanks for the fast collaboration here — apologies for the disruption.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
